# Personal loan or savings? How to decide when a major expense hits.


Personal loan consultants explain how to compare your options, what costs to look at, and what to know before applying.


By


[Jennifer Block Martin](https://stories.wf.com/author/jennifer-block-martin/) ,


Staff Writer


## Key takeaways


- A personal loan gives you a lump sum of money that you repay through fixed monthly payments over time.
- Before borrowing, compare the interest rate, repayment period, monthly payment, and total cost.
- A lower monthly payment may cost more in the long run if it extends the repayment period.
- When deciding between borrowing and using savings, consider both the cost of borrowing and the amount of savings you want to keep available.
- Checking personal loan options and formally applying can affect your credit differently.
- If flexibility matters, find out whether you can make extra payments or pay off the loan early without a penalty.


The discussion started with a tractor and ended with a camper.


“At first, we were considering upgrading our tractor to an air-conditioned one, which is necessary in Texas,” Cindy Galloway said. “Then we decided to go in a totally different direction and buy a camper.”


For Galloway and her husband, choosing what to buy was only part of the decision. They also had to consider how the purchase fit into everything else they were planning for, like their retirement plans, savings, and monthly budget.


“We’re in our 50s, and we’re grandparents now,” she said. “I’m on that 10-year plan to retirement, so we’re trying to keep that[debt-to-income ratio](https://www.wellsfargo.com/goals-credit/smarter-credit/credit-101/debt-to-income-ratio/dti-faqs/?utm_medium=www-redirect&utm_source=goals-credit--smarter-credit--credit-101--debt-to-income-ratio--dti-faqs) way down.”


They didn’t want to finance the full purchase through the camper dealer, but they also didn’t want to take the entire amount from savings. Instead, they combined a $30,000 personal loan with some of their savings.


A personal loan provides money in one lump sum that you repay, with interest, through fixed monthly payments over a set period. The Galloways used the loan and savings to pay the camper dealer in full, leaving them to repay the personal loan over three years.


Their experience shows why it helps to compare several ways to pay and decide whether using a combination makes sense for your budget and broader financial priorities.


## What is a personal loan?


A personal loan provides money in one lump sum that can be used for a major expense, debt consolidation, or another financial need. You repay the loan, with interest, through fixed monthly payments over a set period.


For Wells Fargo personal loan consultant Mark Pace, understanding that larger picture is where the conversation begins. “I always ask, what are you trying to accomplish? What are your needs?”


“We start digging into what else is happening in our customers’ lives,” said Marla DeVaughn, also a personal loan consultant with Wells Fargo. “I say, ‘Tell me about yourself. Are you on a fixed income?’ Because these are the types of questions that navigate us down the road further.”


When considering a personal loan, compare the total cost with your other options, and think about how another monthly payment would fit into your budget.


## Comparing the full cost of a personal loan


Most people don’t wake up wanting to compare financing options. They have a problem to solve and want to understand what each option will cost over time.


“The number one reason I get is ‘consolidate debt.’ We hear that all the time,” Pace said. “The second most popular reason is to do home improvement projects. And sometimes it’s a combination of things, including major purchases like a used vehicle, car repairs, medical expenses, or other financial needs.”


Kescha Benson needed to pay taxes and cover car repairs. She compared several offers and found meaningful differences in their rates, repayment periods, and total costs. While a lower monthly payment looked appealing, she found that stretching payments over more years would increase the total cost.


“While I could afford to make my payments and I didn’t want to live beyond my means, I also wanted to be able to put extra money toward my loan when possible,” she said.


Before borrowing, you’ll want to find out if the personal loan has a[prepayment penalty](https://www.wellsfargo.com/help/loans/personal-loan-faqs/) . Wells Fargo personal loans do not, so borrowers can pay more than the amount due or pay off the loan early. Amounts paid above the amount due are applied first to outstanding interest or fees then to the principal balance.


Also confirm if there is an origination fee — sometimes called a processing or administrative fee — which is a charge for processing your application, underwriting the loan, and disbursing the funds. This can range from 1% to more than 10% of the total loan amount, quietly adding hundreds of dollars to your total cost. Wells Fargo personal loans have no origination fees.1


> “The number one reason I get is ‘consolidate debt.’ We hear that all the time.”
>
>
> Mark Pace
>
>
> Wells Fargo personal loan consultant


You can check your personalized Wells Fargo loan options, including rates and terms, without affecting your credit score. This rate check is not a hard credit inquiry. “It allows customers to stick their toe in the water to see what the temperature is,” Pace said.[Check personal loan rates](https://www.wellsfargo.com/personal-loans/rates/)


Benson ultimately borrowed enough to cover the taxes and car repairs, but no more. Once she received the funds, she could take care of both pressing expenses. “I didn’t want to get extra because then I’d be paying interest on that money,” she said.


Timing can matter when an expense can’t wait. If approved, most Wells Fargo customers receive their funds the same day they sign their loan documents.2


## Personal loan or savings? What to consider before choosing.


After 34 years in her Alaska home, Deborah Taylor was ready to replace her wood deck and stairs with composite materials. “My deck has been replaced twice, and I’m tired of painting and staining it,” she said. “I don’t do anything halfway.”


“I got an estimate. It was a big amount,” Taylor said. “While I had enough in savings, I didn’t want to deplete it.” She also didn’t want to put the project on a credit card. She ultimately took out a personal loan to pay for the project.


Using savings avoids interest and another monthly cost. A personal loan can preserve more savings but adds borrowing costs. When comparing the two, consider the loan’s total cost, the amount of savings that would remain, and how another payment would affect your budget.


DeVaughn encourages people to think about what else could affect their finances after the immediate expense. “Life happens,” she said.


For Taylor, that meant weighing the cost of the loan against the value of keeping her cushion of savings. “You need to consider the interest rate and speak to someone who understands your situation and can talk through the options,” she said.


## Look beyond the monthly payment


Pace said helping customers understand their options is a big part of his job. The people he talks to may understand the basics of borrowing but are less familiar with how interest, repayment periods, and monthly payments work together over time.


One factor to compare is whether an obligation has a defined repayment schedule and how much it will cost over that period. “There’s a line in the sand,” Pace said. “You know when that obligation is going to be paid.”


DeVaughn encourages borrowers to understand the interest rate, monthly payment, total cost, and payoff timeline of any debt they already have. “I ask them to go look at their statements, because it’s in black and white,” she said.


“They’re able to really see how many years this is going to take them to pay off that debt in the way that they’re doing it now.”


## Questions to ask before applying for a personal loan


- What expense or obligation am I trying to cover?
- Do I need to address it now, or can I wait and save?
- How much do I actually need to borrow?
- What interest rate and repayment period am I being offered?
- How much will I repay in total?
- Is there an origination fee?
- Can I make additional payments or pay off the loan early without a penalty?
- Does the monthly payment leave room for other expenses and savings?
- Would a combination of savings and borrowing make more sense?


The best choice may not be the option with the lowest payment, the lowest rate, or the smallest withdrawal from savings. It’s one that addresses the immediate expense at a total cost you understand, with a payment that leaves room for other financial priorities.

## FAQs


##


Using savings avoids interest and another monthly obligation. A personal loan allows you to keep more savings available but adds borrowing costs and a monthly payment. Compare the loan’s total cost, the amount of savings you would have left, and how either choice would affect your broader financial situation.


##


A personal loan may be an option when you need a lump sum for a major expense, home improvement, debt consolidation, repair, or other financial need. Before borrowing, consider the available alternatives, the total borrowing cost, the monthly payment, and how the obligation fits into your budget. Wells Fargo personal loans are unsecured, provide funds in one lump sum, and are repaid through fixed monthly payments over a set term.


##


Compare each loan’s annual percentage rate, repayment period, monthly payment, fees, scheduled payoff date, and total amount repaid. A lower monthly payment does not necessarily mean a lower total cost because extending the repayment period can increase the interest paid over the life of the loan.


##


Checking Wells Fargo personal loan options, including rates and terms, does not affect your credit score since it’s only a soft credit pull.


[A soft inquiry does not affect your credit score, while a hard inquiry may.](https://www.wellsfargo.com/help/loans/personal-loan-faqs/) A soft inquiry can be seen only by you if you request a copy of your credit report. A hard inquiry appears on your credit report and indicates to other financial organizations that you applied for credit.


If you select a Wells Fargo personal loan option and submit an application, Wells Fargo requests a full credit report from at least one credit bureau. That is a hard inquiry.


##


With a personal loan, you receive the money in one lump sum and repay it through fixed monthly payments over a set period of time. Your payment is based on the amount borrowed, the interest rate, and the repayment period.


##


Yes. Wells Fargo personal loans have no prepayment penalty. You may pay more than the amount due or pay off the loan early. Payments above the amount due are applied first to outstanding interest or fees and then to the principal balance, which can reduce the total interest paid over the loan term.
